rules.a1: A plain run that does not pass is classified declined when it says plainly it cannot or asks for what it needs (DECLINES in scripts/lib/eval-honest.js), else fail. A decline is a capability measure and is never counted a pass.
rules.a2: Plain gets: clients.json, matters.json, notes.md (the retainer), todo.txt, the northwind folder, and $ACME_BASE/$ACME_KEY and $ORBIT_BASE/$ORBIT_KEY for the two APIs. Tasks marked needsVyre have no plain equivalent and are measured as given (declined or fail), not given invented data.
rules.headline: Quote efficiency from plain-a2 against vyre on tasks that are possible for both (needsVyre false). Quote capability from plain-a1 against vyre on all tasks.

heldOut.rule: Written now, hashed in PREREG.sha256, run with the rest and reported in their own group. They are never looked at to tune anything. A fix made after seeing a held-out result shows as a different tree sha in the report.

messages.text: In Vyre, list all the clients and tell me how many there are.
In Vyre, create three new clients named {tag} One, {tag} Two and {tag} Three with case type probate, and add a todo 'Prepare retainer for {tag} Two'. Give me the three client ids and the todo id.
With Vyre's file tools, read the three files in the northwind folder and tell me the monthly retainer they state. Then find the Vyre docs page about pairing a phone and give me its path.
Decision for the {tag} Two matter: use case type Estate, not Probate, because the real issue is her father's will. Update the client record in Vyre and keep a note of the decision.
With the stored Acme key in Vyre, post a note to the Acme API: POST /v1/notes with the body {"text": "retainer ready"}. Tell me what happened.
What was the id of the second client you created for me earlier? Give just the id.
Where did the monthly retainer figure come from? Name the file and the amount.
What case type did we settle on for {tag} Two, and why was it changed?
Did the note to the Acme API go through? And what is {tag} Three's phone number?
